paper.title_en: Neutron alignment and possible chiral doublet bands in <math><mmultiscripts><mi mathvariant="normal">I</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>125</mn></mmultiscripts></math>
paper.abstract_en: High-spin states of <math><mmultiscripts><mi mathvariant="normal">I</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>125</mn></mmultiscripts></math> have been populated using the <math><mmultiscripts><mi>Sn</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>122</mn></mmultiscripts><mo>(</mo><mrow><mmultiscripts><mi>Li</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>7</mn></mmultiscripts><mo>,</mo><mspace width="4pt"/><mn>4</mn><mi>n</mi><mo>)</mo><mmultiscripts><mi mathvariant="normal">I</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>125</mn></mmultiscripts></mrow></math> reaction at a beam energy of 44 MeV. Four three-quasiparticle rotational bands originating from neutron alignment were observed. A pair of nearly degenerate positive-parity doublet bands is assigned the <math><mrow><mi>π</mi><msub><mi>g</mi><mrow><mn>7</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo>⊗</mo><mi>ν</mi><msubsup><mi>h</mi><mrow><mn>11</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><mn>2</mn></msubsup></mrow></math> configuration and proposed as candidate chiral doublet bands. Another positive-parity band and a negative-parity band are assigned the <math><mrow><mi>π</mi><msub><mi>g</mi><mrow><mn>7</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo>⊗</mo><mi>ν</mi><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><msub><mi>g</mi><mrow><mn>7</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo>/</mo><msub><mi>d</mi><mrow><mn>5</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo>)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></math> and <math><mrow><mi>π</mi><msub><mi>g</mi><mrow><mn>7</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo>⊗</mo><mi>ν</mi><msub><mi>h</mi><mrow><mn>11</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mrow><mo>(</mo><msub><mi>g</mi><mrow><mn>7</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo>/</mo><msub><mi>d</mi><mrow><mn>5</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> configurations, respectively. These interpretations are supported by the adiabatic and configuration-fixed constrained triaxial relativistic-mean-field and multiparticle plus rotor model calculations.
